submission.natural_language_explanation: Retrospective rare-form detector: the pole fires on the peak token itself when that token is a rare or marked form - a rare CJK/byte token in Japanese or Chinese text ('の�', '田', '五', '王'), a rare mid-word subword fragment ('ribut' in Redistributions, 'umber', 'lor'), a rare capitalised proper noun or technical term (' Odyssey', ' September', ' Virtual', ' Norn'), or a rare legal/technical word ('apache', ' Unless', ' WITHOUT') - inside a formulaic or non-prose passage, above all a full copyright-licence header (BSD, Apache, MIT and GPL headers all fire at 0.1-0.8 of the scan's 0.98 max: the second 'Redistributions' of a BSD clause list, 'apache' in the www.apache.org URL, ' Unless'/' WITHOUT'/' copies' in the warranty clauses), or a formulaic headline, photo caption, title or wiki-markup line ('Mars Odyssey enters orbit around Red Planet', 'Class 108 DTS seen in Manchester Victoria in September 1984'). It stays at baseline on ordinary English prose, on common function words even inside licence headers, on the same rare words placed in plain sentences ('The source code is available', 'The Lord of the Rings', 'The distribution of wealth'), and on generic code identifiers.
